column1: # Pinned, hash-verified, rootless tool installs.  TAB-separated.
# Columns:
#   name  version  min  arch  url  sha256  src:dest[,src:dest...]
# `arch` matches `uname -m`. `src` is a path inside the archive; `dest` is
# relative to $HOME.  A tool with no row for the running architecture is
# skipped with a warning rather than failing.
# `min` is the oldest version that still covers everything this setup uses.
# A system copy (on PATH outside ~/.local/bin) meeting it is preferred:
# `tools install` then skips the pinned download, so distro packages keep
# getting security updates. `--force` overrides; a `min` of `-` never
# accepts a system copy. The floors, with the feature that sets each:
#   fzf       0.48.0   `fzf --zsh` (sourced by the zsh integration);
#                      Debian 13 ships 0.60.3, so its package qualifies
#   uv        0.9.17   relative exclude-newer durations (the `i` launcher)
#   gitleaks  8.19.0   the `stdin` scan command (pre_commit hook)
#   lsd       0.23.1   every flag the listing aliases use, verified against
#                      that binary; Debian 12 (0.23.1) and 13 (1.1.5) qualify
# uv and gitleaks are not packaged by Debian; their floors guard copies
# installed by other means (curl installer, brew, go install). eza (the
# aliases' second-choice backend) is deliberately not pinned: lsd already
# covers the role, so eza is used only when the distro provides it.
# Data, not code, and TAB-separated rather than YAML/TOML on purpose: this is
# read by bash on machines that may have no python and no yq -- including the
# machine that is about to install uv.
# To refresh: bump the version, download the archive, `sha256sum` it, paste.
# `dotfiles tools outdated` prints the current upstream releases.
